components.css: :host{--paper:#f4f6fb;--card:#fff;--field:#e6ecf5;--ink:#122b4a;--soft:#4a5868;--navy:#1a3d66;--deep:#0e2340;--on-dark:#f4f7fb;--on-dark-soft:#c9d7ea;--amber:#f5a623;--amber-2:#ffbb48;--amber-ink:#8a5300;--focus:#1f6fd1;--error:#b3261e;--display:'Cal Sans','Avenir Next','Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif;--text:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI','Helvetica Neue',Arial,sans-serif} .ds-steps{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:28px 20px;display:grid;gap:24px;counter-reset:s;background-color:var(--deep);background-image:repeating-linear-gradient(135deg,transparent 0 22px,rgba(255,255,255,.035) 22px 23px);color:var(--on-dark-soft);font:16px/1.7 var(--text)} .ds-steps li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:48px 1fr;gap:16px;counter-increment:s} .ds-steps li::before{content:counter(s);width:48px;height:48px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;background:var(--amber);color:var(--ink);font:400 20px/1 var(--display)} .ds-steps b{display:block;font:400 21px/1.2 var(--display);color:var(--on-dark);margin-top:4px} .ds-steps span{display:block;margin-top:4px}

narrative.overview:
The site behaves like a good tradesperson on the phone: unhurried, plain, and clear about what happens next. It is Ellie's house calm band style applied to a garage-door company: an off-white paper ground, garage-door navy and deep navy bands, and one safety-amber accent that only ever appears as a fill or as a dedicated darker ink. Full-bleed bands alternate light and dark so each section is obvious on a phone, and nothing on the page competes with the two actions that matter, calling and texting.

Density is low and phone-first. Each band carries one heading, at most one short lede, and one job (the care promise, the service list, three steps, the form, the number). Shapes are soft and borderless; depth comes from band colour, not shadow. Motion is limited to three owner-chosen devices: the hero H1 letter bounce-in, a single 12px fade-up for content below the first screen, and the floating text circle sliding in.

No logo exists, so the palette is chosen rather than extracted: navy for the door, amber for the safety-yellow of a garage door's warning label.
keyCharacteristics: Paper, navy, deep navy, one amber accent; the ground is never black.
Full-bleed alternating bands (paper, navy, deep-with-texture) as the only structural device.
One display webfont (Cal Sans, weight 400) over the system body stack at 16/1.7.
Soft borderless forms: 24px cards, 10px fields, full pills.
Flat surfaces; the only shadow belongs to the floating text circle.

rules.name: The Fill-Only Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber is a fill. Text on amber is Door Ink, never white; amber as text on a light ground switches to Amber Ink. Plain amber text appears only on navy, deep or the hero overlay.

rules.name: The Two-Navy Band Rule
rules.body: Dark bands use exactly two navies: Garage-Door Navy plain, Night Navy with the diagonal line texture (`repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 22px, rgba(255,255,255,.035) 22px 23px)`). The texture stays at about 3.5% white so it never reads as lines through text.

rules.name: The Separate Focus Rule
rules.body: Focus and form-hover outlines use Focus Blue on light grounds, distinct from the amber fill, so a focused amber button still shows a ring. On dark grounds the ring turns amber.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Cal Sans is always weight 400; hierarchy comes from size and band colour, never from bolding the display face. Bold (600) is reserved for short emphasis inside body text.

rules.name: The Accent Phrase Rule
rules.body: A heading may set its last phrase in the accent colour ("What we fix.", "How it works.", the hero's "Fixed in DE, MD, PA & NJ."): amber on dark, Amber Ink on light. One phrase per heading, at the end.

rules.name: The Flat Band Rule
rules.body: Cards, rows, buttons and fields carry no shadow at rest or on hover. If something needs separation, change the ground colour.

dos: Do alternate full-bleed bands (paper, navy, deep-with-texture) so every new section is obvious on a phone.
Do put text on amber in Door Ink, and switch to Amber Ink whenever amber must be text on a light ground.
Do set every heading, button, row and label in Cal Sans 400, and body in the system stack at 16/1.7.
Do keep fields on Field Mist inside white cards, and keep the invalid border red even when focused.
Do outline form controls in Focus Blue on hover and focus; use offset outlines (not borders) on filled chips.
Do use the 12px, 400ms fade-up only for elements that start below the first screen, and leave everything visible without JS or under reduced motion.
Do keep tap targets at 44px or more.
donts: Don't put white text on amber, or plain amber text on paper or white.
Don't add shadows to cards, rows, buttons or fields; the floating text circle is the only lifted element.
Don't animate any heading other than the hero H1.
Don't add a second accent colour, a second body font, or a bold Cal Sans weight.
Don't let an eyebrow pill take a hover state, an arrow, a shadow or a full amber fill.
Don't put two controls that do the same thing in view at once (the floating circle hides over the form).
Don't raise the diagonal band texture above about 4% white.
